title: fix: keep OAuth authorize actions visible on short screens
author: ElliotEtag
pr_body_excerpt:
- Keeps the OAuth consent actions visible by capping the modal to the viewport and scrolling only the consent details.
- Adds opt-in `AuthModal` content classes so other authentication screens keep their current layout.
- Shortens the mobile terms link to `Terms`, retains the full accessible name, and adds the existing external-link cue.
- Validated at 900×529, 375×529, expanded permissions, and 900×720; `npm run typecheck` and `npm run build:frontend` pass.
- Fixes #13451

gist.headline: Consent buttons stay put
gist.blurb: OAuth consent dialogs learned a useful trick: the important buttons now remain in view when a small screen runs out of vertical real estate. The details scroll; the decision does not wander offscreen.
gist.summary: OAuth authorize modals now cap themselves to short viewports and scroll only expanded consent details, keeping Allow and Deny actions visible at 900×529 and mobile-sized screens.
gist.impact: People approving OAuth access on compact screens can review permissions and complete the consent flow without hunting for actions below the fold; mobile terms links now read “Terms” while retaining their full accessible label and external-link cue.
gist.visual_concept: Polli is a careful consent-garden keeper inside a cozy compact OAuth modal, using a tiny tool belt to pin the Allow and Deny buttons safely at the bottom while a tall permissions list scrolls like a flowering vine above them. A small retro monitor robot can hold a readable “TERMS ↗” sign, with pixel flowers and code-plants making the constrained space feel orderly rather than cramped.
